ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a CW317 adjustable voltage regulator circuit, with the input terminal labeled UI and the output terminal labeled Uo. A resistor R1 is connected between the output terminal and the adjustment terminal of the CW317, labeled 150Ω; an adjustable resistor RP is connected between the adjustment terminal and ground, labeled 3kΩ. There are also input and output filter capacitors C1 and C2 on the left and right respectively. Reasoning: The problem states that the input voltage UI is sufficiently large, so the limitation of insufficient dropout voltage is not considered. The approximate output formula of the CW317 adjustable voltage regulator is Uo = 1.25(1 + RP/R1). When RP = 0, Uo = 1.25(1 + 0/150) = 1.25V; when RP = 3kΩ = 3000Ω, Uo = 1.25(1 + 3000/150) = 1.25 × 21 = 26.25V. Therefore the output voltage adjustment range is from 1.25V to 26.25V.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the CW317 output feeds R1 = 150 Ω down to the adjustment node, and RP = 3 kΩ connects that node to ground, forming the DC setting network for Uo. From the text, UI is large enough that saturation/dropout does not constrain Uo. Since the regulator keeps 1.25 V across R1, compute the feedback current I = 1.25/150 A. When RP is adjusted to 0 Ω, the ground-side drop is 0 and Uo = 1.25 V. When RP is adjusted to 3 kΩ, the added drop is I·3000 = 25 V, so Uo = 1.25 + 25 = 26.25 V. Thus the range is 1.25–26.25 V.
